lost_facts.assertion: probe error: TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not TurnLedger (raised inside test_rule__a_versioned_checkpoint_rewritten_after_every_appended_response, at the line `returned = write_sidecar(str(tmp_path), ledger)`)
lost_facts.evidence: The shipped module (msg 157 heredoc) defines `def write_sidecar(ledger: TurnLedger, working_dir: str) -> str` and `def verify_sidecar(ledger: TurnLedger, working_dir: str) -> TurnLedger` — ledger first, working_dir second. The oracle (harbor_tasks/g7-agent-turn-ledger/fixtures/oracle.patch, lines 834-847) and the grader both call `write_sidecar(working_dir, ledger)` — working_dir first, matching the convention every OTHER function in the same ticket/module uses: `read_log(working_dir)`, `load_ledger(working_dir, ...)`, and the agent's own `read_sidecar(working_dir)` (single arg, so order-neutral but still working_dir-first in spirit). At the test's exact call site the mismatch binds tmp_path's string to the agent's `ledger` parameter and the real TurnLedger object to its `working_dir` parameter; internally `sidecar_path(working_dir)` does `os.path.join(working_dir, TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME)` on a TurnLedger instance, producing exactly the observed TypeError. This is a pure self-inconsistency in the agent's own code, not a corpus contradiction: no remark in the answer key's actual dialogue (verified by grep across the full transcript and the raw answer-key 'As it appears' blocks) ever states write_sidecar's or verify_sidecar's argument order in either direction — the phrase 'you hand it the work dir and the ledger' that appears in the answer key's 'What the remark has to leave a reader with' summary for g7.r1.say20 is the task author's paraphrase, not a literal line of dialogue (the actual say20 exchange, lines 1174-1196 of the answer key / grep-verified absent from the transcript, never uses that phrasing). The agent's own Analysis at transcript line 3936 shows it explicitly settling on `verify_sidecar(ledger, work_dir)` mid-run, and then wrote write_sidecar with the same (wrong) order at msg 149-157 without cross-checking against `read_log`/`load_ledger`'s working_dir-first pattern it had itself just implemented and reasoned about at msg 141-149.

search_strategy: Systematic and mostly exhaustive, with one structural gap. Wiki: the agent enumerated pages by keyword (`/api/search?query=...` for agent/seed/resume/multi-turn/curator/completion/tracker), then fetched every matching page WHOLE via `/api/pages/{id}` (script at msg ~85, used repeatedly through steps 12-18, 54-56), which returns body+comments together — exactly the technique the answer key says defeats BookStack's comment-blind search. This recovered essentially all 9 wiki remarks (8 comments + 1 page body: l14, l5, l11, g7r2-l13, g7r2-l14, l2, g7r2-l07, g7r2-l04, g7r2-l10). Chat: the agent wrote a Mattermost dumper (msg ~55, /tmp/mm.py) and ran repeated keyword passes ('ledger', 'sidecar', 'TURN_LEDGER_VERSION', 'sentinel', 'next_speaker', 'interleave', 'status', 'COMPLETION', 'write_sidecar') across ALL channels at once, then read the matching channel files (pipeline.txt, code-review.txt, engineering.txt, incidents.txt, cookbooks.txt, viewer.txt, releases.txt) in windows around the hits. This is thorough but keyword-anchored rather than exhaustive-by-date: remarks whose wording shares none of the searched tokens (g7.r1.l1, g7.r1.say23, g7.r1.fix26, g7.r2.g7r2-l01/l03/l06/l09, g7.r2.say18, the two herring originals) were never located, even though their channels were opened. Mail: subject/body keyword search only ('ledger' -> 12 hits, then 'TurnLedger'/'sentinel'/'next_speaker'/'interleave'/'adopt_ledger'/'num_cached'/'COMPLETION_SENTINEL', lines 2199-2224) — never a full-mailbox enumeration.
